text:
Predicates:
PlayingFor(x, y) ::: x is playing for y.
Brazilian(x) ::: x is Brazilian.
Nautico(y) ::: y is a football club named Nautico.
Braga(y) ::: y is a football club named Braga.
QuestionedClub(y) ::: y is a football club mentioned in the question (e.g., Nautico, Braga).

Premises:
AiltonSilva(bornIn1995) ∧ KnownAs(Ailton, AiltonSilva) ::: Ailton Silva, born in 1995, is known as Ailton.
FootballPlayer(Ailton) ::: Ailton is a football player.
LoanedOut(Ailton, Braga) ::: Ailton was loaned out to Braga.
Brazilian(Ailton) ::: Ailton Silva is a Brazilian footballer.
PlaysFor(Ailton, Nautico) ::: Ailton plays for Nautico.
Nautico(y) ∧ Braga(y) ::: Nautico and Braga are football clubs.
Nautico(y) ::: Nautico is a football club.
Braga(y) ::: Braga is a football club.
Nautico(y) ∧ y ≠ Nautico ::: Nautico is distinct from other clubs like Braga.
Braga(y) ∧ y ≠ Braga ::: Braga is distinct from other clubs like Nautico.

Conclusion:
¬∃x (PlayingFor(x, Nautico) ∧ Brazilian(x)) ::: No one playing for Nautico is Brazilian.
